subjects.name: Applied Chemistry for Fibres, Polymers and Sustainable Textiles
subjects.name_print: Applied Chemistry for Fibres, Polymers and Sustainable Textiles

units.1: Chemistry of Textile Fibres: Classification of textile fibres; natural fibres (cotton, wool, silk, jute) and their chemical composition; synthetic fibres (nylon, polyester, acrylic); physical and chemical properties of fibres; moisture absorption and swelling; fibre morphology and structure-property relationship.
units.2: Polymer Chemistry and Fibre Formation: Introduction to polymers; monomers and polymerization; addition and condensation polymerization, copolymerization, step-growth and chain-growth mechanisms, melt, dry, and wet spinning processes, drawing and orientation, fiber crystallinity and amorphous regions, chemical modification of fibers (graft copolymerization, cross-linking), recycled and bio-based synthetic fibers (PLA, PHA)
units.3: Textile Wet Processing Chemistry: Preparation processes (desizing, scouring, bleaching – chemistry and agents), chemistry of direct, reactive, acid, basic, vat, and disperse dyes, dye-fiber interactions and bonding mechanisms, printing pastes and thickeners, fixation chemistry, after-treatments, water and effluent chemistry in wet processing
units.4: Textile Finishing Chemistry: Mechanical and chemical finishing principles, softeners (anionic, cationic, silicone-based), anti-wrinkle and easy-care finishes (DMDHEU chemistry), water-repellent finishes (fluorocarbon, C6 vs C8), flame-retardant finishes (halogenated and phosphorus-based), UV protection finishes, nanotechnology in textile finishing
units.5: Sustainable and Functional Textile Chemistry: Environmental issues in textile industry,Green chemistry in textile processing, biodegradable dyes and natural dyes, enzyme-based processes (amylases, cellulases, proteases), antimicrobial textiles (silver nanoparticles, chitosan, zinc oxide), phase-change materials in textiles, e-textiles chemistry, recycling of textile waste, circular economy in textile industry

Understand polymer chemistry principles to analyze fiber formation and chemical modification
Implement dye-fiber chemistry and wet processing to optimize textile coloration processes
Describe finishing chemistry to design functional textile properties such as water repellency and flame retardancy
Understand green chemistry and sustainable practices to textile processing and functional textile design

subjects.name: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering

units.1: Basic Electrical Quantities and DC Circuits: Basic concepts of Electric charge, current, voltage, resistance, power, and energy; Ohm's law; series and parallel combination of resistors; Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) and Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL); Thevenin's theorem (simple concept and problem). simple mesh and nodal analysis.
units.2: Single-Phase AC Circuits and Power: AC voltage and current — peak, RMS, average values; phasor representation; R, L, and C circuits and their series and parallel connections; admittance and impedance; active power (P), reactive power (Q), apparent power (S); power factor and its significance; power factor correction using shunt capacitors; single-phase power measurement using wattmeter.
units.3: Unit III – Three-Phase Systems: Three phase power supply and loads, balanced star and delta connections; phase and line voltages and currents; three-phase power; two-wattmeter method.
units.4: Unit IV – Transformers and Electrical Machines: Working principle of single-phase transformer; EMF equation; voltage and current ratio; losses and efficiency; concept of step-up and step-down transformer; Equivalent circuit and phasor diagram (no load condition). DC motor — types, working principle, back EMF, torque; three-phase induction motor — rotating magnetic field, slip, torque-speed curve, starting (DOL and star-delta).
units.5: Unit V – Electrical Safety and Emerging applications: Electrical hazards — shock and fire; earthing and grounding; working principle of fuses and circuit breakers; electrical safety in laboratory; Applications: Working of fluorescent lamps; motor used in water pumps, lathe machines; key components of energy bills.

subjects.name: Introduction to Indian Knowledge System

units.1:
Foundations of the Indian Knowledge System
Definition, scope, characteristics and significance of IKS; the IKS vision of NEP 2020; the fourteen (Chaturdasha) Vidyasthanas — four Vedas, four Upavedas and six Vedangas; Schools of Indian Philosophy: Orthodox and Heterodox Schools; Oral and Written Knowledge Systems, Knowledge validation (pramanas).
Case study: relevance of IKS for a present-day engineer.
units.2:
Indian Mathematics, Astronomy and Scientific Thinking
Number Systems: Decimal place-value system, zero and infinity; Bhutasankhya and Katapayadi numeration; Pingala’s Chandahshastra and binary representation; Sulbasutras; contributions of Aryabhata, Brahmagupta, Bhaskara and the Kerala School; Indian astronomy and the Panchanga.
Numerical: encoding numbers using the Katapayadi scheme/Observing Panchang and Reflecting on the Patterns
units.3:
Engineering, Technology and Material Sciences
Metallurgy — Wootz steel, zinc distillation and the Delhi Iron Pillar; town planning and architecture (Harappan, Vastu and Shilpa Shastra); water management — stepwells, tanks and irrigation, textile engineering
Case study: materials-science analysis of the Iron Pillar/ Architecture of Stupas
units.4:
Health, Wellness, Environment and Governance
Ayurveda (Charaka and Sushruta), Tridosha; Yoga (Patanjali’s Ashtanga) and wellness; environment and sustainability in Indian thought; governance and management — Kautilya’s Arthashastra; ethics from the Bhagavad Gita.
Case study: Yoga for well-being / Arthashastra management principles/ Learnings from Geeta
units.5:
Contemporary Relevance, AI and Applications of IKS
Digital preservation (CSIR-TKDL, IKS Division) and IPR; Sanskrit and computational linguistics — Panini’s Ashtadhyayi, NLP and AI for ancient texts; IKS-inspired sustainable engineering and innovation.
Case study: AI/NLP applied to a Sanskrit corpus.

subjects.name: Introduction to AI and Prompt Engineering
subjects.name_print: Introduction to AI and Prompt Engineering

units.1:
1. Definition and scope of AI; brief history — from Alan Turing to ChatGPT
2. Types of AI — Narrow AI, General AI, Super AI (concept)
3. AI vs Machine Learning vs Deep Learning — what is the difference
4. How machines learn — data, patterns, and predictions (concept, no maths)
5. AI today — where it already exists in daily life (Google Maps, Spotify, Netflix, Google Photos, voice assistants)
6. Machine Learning Concepts, Learning Strategies- Supervised, Unsupervised, Reinforcement Learning
7. Data, Data Visualization, Data Pre-processing
Class Activity: Students list 5 AI tools they use every day and discuss how each one 'learns'.
Branch connect: CE — AI in structural health monitoring; ME — AI in predictive maintenance; EE — smart grid; CSE — AI in compilers; BT — drug discovery; AG — crop yield prediction.
units.2:
1. Machine learning: Classification Techniques- K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Naïve Bayes, Clustering Technique-K-Means
2. Classification metrics-accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, MAE.
3. Neural networks — concept of neurons, layers, weights (simple diagram)
4. Deep learning — what makes it 'deep'; why it needs GPUs, CNN
5. Computer vision — how AI sees images (face recognition, medical imaging)
6. Natural Language Processing (NLP) — how AI understands text and speech
Class Activity: Show Google Teachable Machine (teachablemachine.withgoogle.com) — train a simple image classifier in 5 minutes, no code.
Branch connect: ECE — image sensors + AI; BT — protein structure prediction (AlphaFold); AG — plant disease detection from photos; TX — fabric defect detection.
units.3:
1. What is Generative AI — AI that creates text, images, code, audio, video
2. Large Language Models (LLMs) — what they are, how they are trained (concept)
3. Popular LLMs — ChatGPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google), Claude (Anthropic), Llama (Meta)
4. Tokens, context window, temperature — simple explanation
5. Multimodal AI — text + image + voice in one model (GPT-4o, Gemini concept)
6. AI image generation — Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, DALL-E (concept + demo)
7. Limitations of LLMs — hallucination, knowledge cutoff, bias
8. Responsible use — academic integrity, plagiarism, AI-generated content disclosure
Class Activity: Students interact with ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude; observe how different inputs give different outputs; identify one hallucination example.
Every professional today uses at least one Generative AI tool. Understanding how LLMs work makes students better users and future developers.
units.4:
1. AI in Civil Engineering — structural health monitoring, smart cities, traffic optimisation
2. AI in Mechanical Engineering — predictive maintenance, design optimisation, robotics
3. AI in Electrical and Electronics — smart grids, fault detection, VLSI design automation
4. AI in CSE — code generation (GitHub Copilot), cybersecurity, natural language interfaces
5. AI in Biotechnology and Healthcare — drug discovery, medical imaging, genomics, wearables
6. AI in Agricultural Engineering — precision farming, crop monitoring, drone-based spraying, soil analysis
7. AI in Chemical and Textile Engineering — process optimisation, quality control, material design
8. Ethical concerns — bias in AI, data privacy, job displacement, responsible AI
Class Activity: One case study per student group — each group presents a 2-minute real AI application from their own engineering branch.
This unit ensures every student, regardless of branch, sees AI as directly relevant to their future career.
units.5:
1. What is a prompt — the instruction you give to an AI model
2. Why prompt quality matters — same AI, very different results with different prompts
3. Principles of good prompting — clarity, context, specificity, role assignment, format instruction
4. Prompting techniques:     • Zero-shot prompting — direct question     • Few-shot prompting — give examples in the prompt     • Chain-of-thought prompting — ask AI to think step by step     • Role prompting — 'Act as a civil engineer and...'
5. Prompt for different tasks — summarisation, explanation, code generation, report writing, brainstorming, translation
6. Domain-specific prompting — students write prompts relevant to their own branch (CE, ME, BT, AG, etc.)
7. AI tools for engineers — GitHub Copilot (code), Grammarly (writing), Consensus (research), Wolfram Alpha, Canva AI, Notion AI
Hands-on Practice (every lecture): Students write prompts, compare outputs, refine and improve.
Graded prompt assignment: write 5 prompts for an engineering problem from their own branch.
Prompt Engineering is already a job role (avg. salary $100K+ globally). Every engineer who can communicate well with AI has a significant career advantage.

cos.text: Explain what AI is, its types, and identify AI applications in everyday life and their own engineering domain
Describe key AI concepts — ML, Deep Learning, NLP, Computer Vision — and relate them to real applications
Apply the working principles, capabilities, limitations, and responsible use of Generative AI and Large Language Models.
Apply the concept of Artificial Intelligence across engineering domains and their societal, ethical, and professional implications.
Design and refine effective prompts using zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, and role prompting techniques for domain-specific tasks

objectives_print: 1. Understand what Artificial Intelligence is, its history, and how it is changing every engineering field
2. Understand key AI concepts — Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Neural Networks — at a conceptual level

experiments.exp: Fibre Identification by Chemical Solubility Tests - Identify given natural and synthetic fibre samples (cotton, wool, silk, nylon, polyester, acrylic) using differential solubility in acids, alkalis, and solvents; record systematic observations

Moisture Regain and Moisture Content of Fibres - Determine moisture regain and moisture content of cotton, wool, nylon, and polyester samples by oven-drying method; relate to hygroscopicity and comfort properties of fibres

Viscosity Average Molecular Weight of Polymer - Measure viscosity of polymer solution (PVA or cellulose) at different concentrations using Ostwald viscometer; determine intrinsic viscosity [η]; compute viscosity-average molecular weight using Mark-Houwink equation
Degree of Polymerisation by Viscosity Method - Determine degree of polymerisation (DP) of a cellulose or polymer sample from intrinsic viscosity; relate DP to fibre strength and processing behaviour

Dyeing of Cotton with Direct Dye - Dye a cotton fabric sample with a direct dye at optimum temperature and salt concentration; measure dye exhaustion by UV-Vis spectrophotometry; calculate % exhaustion and colour strength (K/S value)
Dyeing of Nylon with Acid Dye - Dye a nylon fabric with an acid dye under acidic conditions; control pH with acetic acid; measure exhaustion by UV-Vis; study effect of pH on dye uptake
Effluent Analysis of Dye Bath - Analyse the exhausted dye bath effluent for BOD, COD, and colour; relate to environmental impact of textile wet processing; assess need for treatment

Softener Finish – Effect on Fabric Handle - Apply cationic softener to cotton fabric at different concentrations; evaluate handle by subjective bending test and crease recovery angle measurement; relate to softener chemistry

Water Repellency Test on Finished Fabric - Apply water-repellent finish (fluorocarbon or silicone-based) to fabric samples; evaluate water repellency by spray test (IS/AATCC method) and contact angle measurement; relate to DWR chemistry

Natural Dye Extraction and Dyeing - Extract natural dye from turmeric, henna, or onion skin; mordant cotton fabric with alum; dye and assess colour strength by UV-Vis; relate to sustainable natural dyeing and green textile chemistry

Enzymatic Scouring of Cotton (Bio-scouring Demo) - Scour cotton fabric using pectinase enzyme solution; compare whiteness, wettability, and weight loss with conventional alkali scouring; relate to enzyme-based green processing

Burning Test and Melting Behaviour of Fibres - Perform burning test on natural (cotton, wool, silk) and synthetic (nylon, polyester, acrylic) fibres; observe flame behaviour, odour, and ash; correlate with fibre chemical structure and fire safety

cos.text: Apply engineering drawing standards and conventions (BIS/ISO) while setting up and dimensioning a drawing.
Construct orthographic and sectional views of points, lines, planes and solids using a CAD package.
Develop surfaces and isometric views of solids, read given views to visualise the object, and apply this to draw textile machine components, weave-design diagrams and mill layouts.

re-extracted from detail page p.76 (B37 verify repair)

experiments.exp:
Drawing standards, sheet layout and the CAD environment
Sheet sizes, borders, title block, lines, lettering and dimensioning as per BIS conventions (SP 46 : 2003 (BIS) Engineering Drawing Practice for Schools and Colleges; IS 10711 (sheet sizes and layout); IS 9609 (lettering); IS 10714 (line conventions); IS 11669 (preparation of general engineering drawings); ISO 128 series.). Familiarisation with the CAD interface: coordinate entry, units, limits, object snap, layers, line types and file management.
Students set up a standard A3/A4 template with a title block that will be reused throughout the semester.

Geometric constructions and engineering curves
Construction of polygons, tangents, plain and diagonal scales; conic sections (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) and one roulette (cycloid or involute) using CAD draw and modify commands (LINE, ARC, OFFSET, TRIM, ARRAY, MIRROR). Stream context: cam profiles of a tappet shedding mechanism, the helix of yarn twist on a package, and the cycloidal traverse of a builder motion.

Orthographic projection of points and straight lines
Projections of points in the four quadrants; projections of lines inclined to one and both reference planes; true length and true inclination by rotation/trapezoidal method. Principal planes handled on separate CAD layers.

Orthographic projection of planes and simple solids
First angle projection of planes and of prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones resting in given positions; front, top and side views. Third angle convention introduced for comparison, since it is common in imported drawings.

Sections of solids and true shape of section
Solids cut by section planes perpendicular to one reference plane and inclined to the other; sectional views, cutting plane line, hatching conventions and true shape of the section obtained by auxiliary projection.

Development of lateral surfaces
Parallel line and radial line development of cube, prism, cylinder, cone and truncated solids. Stream context: development of a cone/cheese package surface, a conical funnel of a fibre transport duct and a sheet metal machine guard.

Isometric projection and reading of orthographic views
Isometric scale, isometric axes and isometric drawing aids in CAD; conversion of given orthographic views into an isometric view, and the reverse exercise of reading a pictorial view and producing orthographic views. Missing line and missing view problems for visualisation practice.

Drawing of a textile machine component
Orthographic and sectional drawing of a machine part, a ring frame spindle with bolster and wharve, a heald and reed section, a shuttle, a tappet/cam profile or a drafting roller with its bearing. The cam profile is plotted from the displacement diagram rather than copied, so that the link between motion requirement and geometry is visible.

Weave design: point paper design, draft and peg plan
Preparation of point paper (design paper) representations of plain, twill, satin/sateen and a simple derivative weave, together with the corresponding drafting plan and peg/lifting plan, drawn on a CAD grid using ARRAY and layer control; cross sectional views of the fabric structure along warp and weft. A colour and weave effect is produced for one design.

3D modelling of a textile component
Solid model of a component such as a bobbin, cone, cot/apron roller or a package holder arm, using revolve/extrude/sweep features; automatic generation of orthographic and sectional views from the model.

Garment pattern block, mill layout, sheet composition and plotting
Drafting of a basic bodice/sleeve block to given measurements with grain lines, notches and seam allowances; and a machine layout plan of a spinning or weaving shed showing machine positions, passages, material flow and clearances. Composition of a complete sheet with title block; plotting to scale and export to PDF/DXF.

Mini project with an introduction to textile CAD/CAM and AI tools
In groups of two or three, students deliver either a machine component drawing set (detail plus assembly, with 3D model) or a design set (weave/print design with fabric cross sections and a pattern block). The session includes a demonstration of jacquard/dobby design software, digital printing workflows, 3D garment simulation, and AI assisted print/weave design generation and defect detection. Evaluation by presentation and viva voce.

objectives_print: 1. To familiarise the student with the principles, conventions and standards of engineering drawing, so that a drawing can be read and prepared without ambiguity.
2. To develop the ability to visualise a three-dimensional object and to represent it through orthographic, sectional and pictorial views.
3. To develop working competence in a CAD package for two-dimensional drafting and for basic three-dimensional modelling.
4. To develop the ability to prepare drawings of the components, systems and layouts that occur in the Textile Engineering Stream (TX), rather than generic examples.
5. To develop the ability to prepare drawings of textile machine components, fabric design diagrams and mill layouts, and to introduce textile specific CAD as used in the industry.

subjects.name: Environment & Sustainability

units.1: Environment and Ecosystems: Environment — definition, components (atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, biosphere); ecosystem — structure and function; food chain, food web, energy flow (basic concept); biodiversity — meaning, importance, and threats; need for conservation. Awareness focus: local ecosystems and why they matter.
units.2: Natural Resources and their Conservation: Renewable and non-renewable resources; water resources — scarcity and conservation; forest and land resources; energy resources (brief); over-exploitation of resources; the concept of the 3 R's — Reduce, Reuse, Recycle; rainwater harvesting (concept). Awareness focus: simple resource-saving practices in daily life.
units.3: Environmental Pollution: Air pollution — causes, effects, control (basic); water pollution — sources, effects, prevention; soil pollution; noise pollution; solid waste management — segregation, composting, recycling; e-waste and plastic waste (awareness). Awareness focus: pollution in the student's own city/campus and how to reduce it.
units.4: Climate Change and Sustainable Development: Global warming and greenhouse effect (simple explanation); climate change — causes and impacts; carbon footprint (concept + how to reduce); sustainable development — definition and need; UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) — overview of the 17 goals; renewable energy — solar, wind, biomass (awareness level). Awareness focus: calculating and reducing one's own carbon footprint.
units.5: Environmental Protection, Law and the Role of Engineers: Environmental protection measures; brief overview of environmental laws in India (Environment Protection Act, Water Act, Air Act — awareness only, no legal detail); role of individuals, society, and technology in environmental protection; green campus and green buildings (concept); role of engineers in sustainable design and clean technology; environmental ethics. Awareness focus: how each engineering branch can contribute to sustainability.

experiments.exp: Diffraction grating - To determine the wavelength of different spectral lines of mercury light using plane transmission grating.
He -Ne Laser - To determine the wavelength of He-Ne laser light using single slit diffraction.
Polarimeter - To determine the specific rotation of cane sugar solution using polarimeter.
Nodal Slide - To determine the focal length of the combination of two lenses separated by a distance and verify the formula for the focal length of combination of lenses.
Planck's constant - To determine Planck's constant using photoelectric effect.
Optical Fiber - To measure attenuation in an optical fiber.
Stefan’s Law - To verify Stefan’s law by electric method.
Energy Band Gap - To determine the energy band gap of a given semiconductor material.
Hall Effect - To study Hall effect and determine Hall coefficient, carrier density and mobility of a given semiconductor material using Hall effect setup.
Variation of Magnetic Field - To determine the variation of magnetic field with the distance along the axis of a current carrying coil and estimate the radius of the coil.
B-H Curve - To draw hysteresis curve (B-H curve) of a specimen in the form of a transformer and to determine its hysteresis loss.
Carey Foster's Bridge - To determine resistance per unit length and specific resistance of a given resistance using Carey Foster's Bridge.
Electrochemical Equivalent - To determine the electrochemical equivalent (ECE) of copper.
Coefficient of Viscosity - To determine the coefficient of viscosity of a given liquid.
Surface Tension - To measure surface tension of a liquid (e.g., water, ethanol, and surfactant solutions) at room temperature using capillary rise or stalagmometer.
Compound Pendulum - To determine the value of acceleration due to gravity (g) using compound pendulum.
Moment of Inertia - To determine the moment of inertia of a flywheel about its own axis of rotation.
Young’s Modulus - To determine the Young’s Modulus of a material by Searle's apparatus.
Franck-Hertz Experiment - To determine the first excitation potential of a gas (e.g. Argon) by Franck-Hertz experiment and verify discrete nature of atomic energy transitions.
Solar Cell - To study the characteristics of a solar cell.
Characteristics of Logic Gates - To study the switching characteristics of fundamental logic gates constructed using transistors (BJT/MOSFET), measure propagation delay and power dissipation.

Fibre Identification by Chemical Solubility Tests - Identify given natural and synthetic fibre samples (cotton, wool, silk, nylon, polyester, acrylic) using differential solubility in acids, alkalis, and solvents; record systematic observations

Moisture Regain and Moisture Content of Fibres - Determine moisture regain and moisture content of cotton, wool, nylon, and polyester samples by oven-drying method; relate to hygroscopicity and comfort properties of fibres

Viscosity Average Molecular Weight of Polymer - Measure viscosity of polymer solution (PVA or cellulose) at different concentrations using Ostwald viscometer; determine intrinsic viscosity [η]; compute viscosity-average molecular weight using Mark-Houwink equation
Degree of Polymerisation by Viscosity Method - Determine degree of polymerisation (DP) of a cellulose or polymer sample from intrinsic viscosity; relate DP to fibre strength and processing behaviour

Dyeing of Cotton with Direct Dye - Dye a cotton fabric sample with a direct dye at optimum temperature and salt concentration; measure dye exhaustion by UV-Vis spectrophotometry; calculate % exhaustion and colour strength (K/S value)
Dyeing of Nylon with Acid Dye - Dye a nylon fabric with an acid dye under acidic conditions; control pH with acetic acid; measure exhaustion by UV-Vis; study effect of pH on dye uptake
Effluent Analysis of Dye Bath - Analyse the exhausted dye bath effluent for BOD, COD, and colour; relate to environmental impact of textile wet processing; assess need for treatment
Softener Finish – Effect on Fabric Handle
